viscosityPipe.title: Viscosity & Pipe Flow
viscosityPipe.description: Investigate Poiseuille's law in laminar flow, parabolic velocity profile, Reynolds dye streak experiment, and transition to turbulence.

viscosityPipe.theoryContent:
Poiseuille's Law:
For steady, laminar, incompressible flow of a Newtonian fluid through a cylindrical pipe, volumetric flow rate scales with the fourth power of pipe radius and pressure drop, inversely proportional to dynamic viscosity and length:
Q = (π R⁴ ΔP) / (8 η L)

Parabolic Velocity Profile & No-Slip Condition:
Due to intermolecular viscous shear at boundaries, fluid velocity equals zero at the pipe wall (no-slip condition) and rises parabolically to a centerline maximum (v_max = 2 v_avg).

Reynolds Number & Regimes:
The dimensionless Reynolds number quantifies the ratio of inertial to viscous forces: Re = ρ v D / η.
- Re < 2300: Laminar flow (smooth parallel streamlines, razor-sharp Reynolds dye filament).
- 2300 ≤ Re ≤ 4000: Transition flow (wavy streak, vortex shedding onset).
- Re > 4000: Turbulent flow (chaotic eddies, rapid mixing, blunted velocity profile).

Temperature Dependence of Viscosity:
Increasing liquid temperature weakens intermolecular cohesion, exponentially decreasing dynamic viscosity.
